evidence.title: Quoting The New York Times
evidence.excerpt: Anthropic detailed the activity of its A.I. agents in a blog post on Friday, without naming the targeted websites. But two sources with knowledge of the incidents said Anthropic’s A.I. agents had submitted 20 visa applications through a form available on the State Department’s website. All the applications were incomplete and were not processed, they said. — The New York Times , Anthropic Agents Tried to Fill Out Visa Forms on State Dept. evidence.title: What is Codemode
evidence.excerpt:
More than a year ago I wrote a few posts here that recommended people not to load custom tools into their context (or MCP servers) but to just use more scripts.
[…]
However bash has one fundamental limitation which is that it can only compose programs that run.
[…]
If a multimodal model needs to read an image, it cannot use cat for that because the harness needs to inject the actual image payload into the protocol of the LLM.
[…]
In order to spawn and orchestrate sub agents, it’s tricky to avoid tools that are provided by the harness. While in theory the agent could provide a CLI tool that talks to the outer harness via environment variables and Unix sockets, it’s a rather crude process.

evidence.title: Anthropic is cutting off its internal evaluations from the internet
evidence.excerpt: After a recent spate of high-profile incidents in which AI agents escaped containment, Anthropic is cutting off internet access for all internal evaluations. In a report Friday, the company detailed "unintended model actions," including submitting a false tip regarding an unsolved murder, that led to the decision. Although the impact of these behaviors was minimal […]

evidence.title: Show HN: I used Claude Code to address the HN comments on my 2019 game
evidence.excerpt:
In 2019 I posted Aim and Shoot here, a browser shooter where every enemy is a neural network evolved by a genetic algorithm between rounds: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=21353123 The thread had a lot of good feedback that I never got around to.
[…]
This year I gave Claude Code the thread and the repo and worked through it: - "Give the player full health every round" (four of you asked): done.
[…]
- "I wish there was a scoreboard, I wanted a screenshot of how far I got": the game-over screen now shows the round you reached and your best.
[…]
- "The gun sound is jarring": quieter, and M mutes it.
[…]
It's PHP + SQLite on a small VPS, with a local fallback if the server is down.
